subject: Mutual action plan: acceptance signals, cost ladder & owners
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@edgescale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + MAP proposal (acceptance signals, KPIs, owners)

Hi Samir / Priya (cc'd on follow-ups),

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on the problem set and where Redwood can help on latency-sensitive summarization for EdgeScale's agent pipeline. I promised a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a concrete set of success signals so we can scope the pilot and speed up procurement. Attached: EdgeScale_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + milestones).

High-level proposal (three-week sandbox trial):
- Goal: Validate production-quality inference with sub-250ms P95 latency for 2k concurrent users and acceptable unit economics.
- Duration: 3 weeks of instrumented testing + 1-week readout

Acceptance signals (proposed):
1) Latency: P95 <= 250 ms for end-to-end gen on our default prompt shape (see attachment) during steady-state 50 RPS test window.
2) Throughput: Sustained 50 requests/sec with <5% error rate; peak bursts to 120 RPS handled by autoscale with <20% latency degradation.
3) Cost: Effective cost per 1k tokens <= $1.50 (i.e., cost/token <= $0.0015) with recommended batching/quantization profile.
4) Quality: Human-eval pass rate >= 85% on a 500-sample blind evaluation set (precision-focused).
5) Reliability: No production-impacting errors during the trial; successful graceful fallback to smaller model variant for 95th percentile of requests when capacity constrained.

Evaluation plan / instrumentation:
- Week 0 (kickoff): data ingest checklist, baseline benchmark with your sample workload (10k tokens/day toy -> ramp).
- Week 1: Load shaping + KV/prefix caching enabled; measure P95/P99 and token throughput.
- Week 2: End-to-end integration tests with agent pipeline; collect human-eval samples.
- Week 3: Final runbook: cost per token analysis + runbook for escalation.

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood: Ben (sales) — MAP owner / procurement liaison; Karthik (performance) — bench runs & tuning; Marissa (CS) — onboarding + eval instrumentation.
- EdgeScale: Samir — product owner (KPIs); Priya — infra contact (access/VMs/security).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Confirm the acceptance signals above (or propose changes) by Thurs, 5/27.
2) Approve proposed owner assignments so we can lock kickoff calendar.
3) Provide the secure S3 link or sample payload (anonymized) for baseline runs.

If this looks good I will attach a short SLO draft and slot a 30-min kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: EdgeScale_MAP_v1.xlsx
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@edgescale.com>

Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@edgescale.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + MAP proposal (acceptance signals, KPIs, owners)

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. This is mostly aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifying items from our infra team before we sign off:  

- For the latency target, can you confirm measurement window (steady-state 60s or 5m rolling)? Our traffic has microbursts and we care about 5m windows.
- For throughput: our on-prod agent fanout can hit short bursts of 200-250 RPS. You mentioned autoscale — what's the expected warmup time and fallback model characteristics?
- Cost: the $0.0015/token baseline looks reasonable, but we need to see an example calculation showing default batch sizes and quantization settings that achieve it.

Also need to confirm compliance constraints: can Redwood host the sandbox in our VPC or will this be hosted? If hosted, we need SOC2 evidence and data retention policy for the trial.

We can aim to confirm acceptance signals by Friday (5/28) if you can provide the SLO draft and the warmup/canary plan.

cc: Priya (infra) — looping you for inputs on warmup and S3 access.

—Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Product, EdgeScale Inc.
samir.gupta@edgescale.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-24T13:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + MAP proposal (acceptance signals, KPIs, owners)

Hi Samir / Priya — thanks for the quick review and great questions. I pulled together the canary and instrumentation plan below and attached a short SLO draft (slo-proposal.md).

Canary & measurement notes:
- Measurement window: we'll report rolling 5-minute P95 and P99, plus a 60s steady-state snapshot for burst characterization.
- Warmup: autoscale warmup targeted at 90s; we recommend a staged canary (10% traffic -> 30% -> 100% over ~20 minutes) to observe cache-warm behavior.
- Fallback: when capacity headroom < 15% we shift to a smaller compatible model variant; fallback path is tested in week-2 runs.

Bench assumptions for cost calc (example):
- Default batch size: dynamic batching tuned to median sequence length (40 tokens).
- Quantization: INT8 variant for production-run cost baseline; yields ~25-30% token-cost reduction versus FP16 in our tests.
- Example: at 50 RPS, 300 tokens/req average, we estimate cost ~ $1.30 per 1k tokens under the INT8 profile. Full calc in the attachment.

Owners & immediate actions: 
- Karthik: will run baseline bench and produce a tuning sheet (target date: Tue 5/31).
- Marissa: will create the eval harness and human-eval rubric and coordinate access (target date: Wed 6/2).
- Ben: will coordinate procurement and finalize MAP milestones.

I'll propose two 30-min slots for kickoff next week. If you can share the anonymized payload (S3 link) and SOC2 copy I can get the wheels moving.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: slo-proposal.md
